The reasoning shows that every column must be traversed by moving from one extreme row to the opposite extreme (0 ↔ 2) with the middle row visited in between, because vertical moves are only allowed between adjacent rows. Consequently the exit row of each column must be opposite to its entry row, forcing the sequence of exit rows to alternate 2, 0, 2, 0,… starting at 2 and ending at 0. This determines the whole \(y\)-sequence uniquely; the only remaining freedom is the choice of the starting column \(a\) (20 possibilities). Hence there are exactly \(20\) valid permutations.

The proposed solution’s count of 1100 vastly overestimates the possibilities, so the final answer is not correct.
